name: specwarden-workspace
description: A repository declares its rules; specwarden proves which hold. The workspace root — every package lives beside it.

scripts.//scaffold: Package manifests, build configs and READMEs are DERIVED from scripts/registry.mjs. Edit the registry and regenerate: a direct edit to a generated file is overwritten, deliberately.
scripts.//check:drift: Generated output against its registry. A hand edit does not survive the next scaffold run, and the window between the two is where a wrong version or a missing `files` entry ships to npm.
scripts.//check:lockfile: The lockfile against the manifests, which is what CI installs with. `--lockfile-only` touches no node_modules, so it costs a fraction of a second and catches the rename that nothing local re-read.
scripts.//check:publishable: Publish readiness: name, version, licence, repository address, files, private cleared. Separate from the build because the window to unpublish is 72 hours and there is no second one.
scripts.//check:router: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are one router under two names. --write regenerates the mirror.
scripts.//check:skills: The shipped skills and the marketplace that lists them. Nobody here reads either, which is why they rot — a dead entry is invisible to us and total for the agent that followed it.
scripts.//test: Sequential, and ENFORCED rather than merely described: `pnpm -r` runs four packages at a time by default, and each vitest already fans out across every core. Two heavy suites at once is how a run dies with a terminated worker rather than an assertion.
scripts.//test:scripts: The repository's own guard scripts. They are not workspace packages, so `pnpm -r` does not reach them.
scripts.//verify:build: Installs the built tarballs into a temporary project and imports from them. `dist/index.js exists` proves a file exists; this proves a consumer can use it.
scripts.//check: The whole list, both tiers, through the engine. It used to be a hand-kept chain of eleven scripts beside `pnpm gate`, and the chain had already fallen behind: `package-playgrounds` and `playgrounds` were gates and not in it, so `pnpm release` — which ran the chain — could ship over both. One list; this is it.
scripts.//release: Publishes every package to npm. The order is the point: everything is checked, then the whole chain is built and verified, then the packages go — so a manual release cannot skip what CI runs for it. Add --otp=<code> when the account has 2FA.
scripts.release: pnpm run check && node scripts/check-publishable.mjs --releasing && pnpm -r publish --access public
scripts.//gate: The repository, checked by the engine it publishes. This is the check list; the scripts under scripts/ are the logic its checks wrap.
